title: Quasi-finiteness along the finite component of a fibre
statement: Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a ring map of finite type ($B$ a finitely generated $A$-algebra), let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal and $IB$ the ideal of $B$ generated by $\varphi(I)$. Suppose $B/IB=C_1\times C_2$ is a product of rings with $C_1$ finite over $A/I$, i.e. a finitely generated $A/I$-module via $A/I\to B/IB\to C_1$. Let $\varepsilon\in B/IB$ be the idempotent $(1,0)$, so that $C_1=\varepsilon(B/IB)$ with identity $\varepsilon$, and let $\pi:B\to C_1$, $b\mapsto\varepsilon\bar b$, be the composite of $B\to B/IB$ with the projection. Let $T\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] be the set of primes $\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak P)$, $\mathfrak P$ a prime ideal of $C_1$ (the image of $\operatorname{Spec}(C_1)$ in $\operatorname{Spec}(B)$; it consists of primes containing $IB$). Then for every $\mathfrak q\in T$, with $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ and residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], the ring map $A\to B$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]: the prime of the fibre ring $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q$ is an isolated point of $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p))$. This is the affine notion referred to in [pqf-def-quasifinite] (1) (Stacks Algebra, Definition 10.122.3, Tag 00PL, with condition (1) of Lemma 10.122.2, Tag 00PK).

source.place: literature/stacks-project/more-algebra.tex:2512-2516, proof of Lemma Tag 09XH (lemma-helper-finite-type): quasi-finite at every prime of T by looking at fibre rings; the affine definition/criterion are Algebra Tags 00PK and 00PM

proof.text: Set-up. Let $\mathfrak q\in T$, say $\mathfrak q=\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak P)$ with $\mathfrak P\subset C_1$ prime, and $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Since $\pi$ vanishes on $IB$, $IB\subseteq\mathfrak q$; for $a\in I$, $\varphi(a)\in IB\subseteq\mathfrak q$, so $a\in\mathfrak p$: $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Choose $u\in B$ whose class in $B/IB$ is $1-\varepsilon$; then $\pi(u)=\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)=0\in\mathfrak P$, so $u\in\mathfrak q$. Put $F=B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $j:B\to F$, $b\mapsto b\otimes1$.

source.place: more-algebra.tex:2512-2516, proof of Lemma Tag 09XH (lemma-helper-finite-type), first sentence ('by looking at fibre rings, see Algebra, Definition 00PL'); details written out by the worker

proof.text: The map $\rho:B/IB\to F$. The structure map $A\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)=A_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] sends $a\in\mathfrak p$ to the class of $a/1\in\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$, i.e. to $0$; as $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$ (step 1) it kills $I$. Hence for $a\in I$, $b\in B$: $j(\varphi(a)b)=\varphi(a)b\otimes1=b\otimes(a\cdot1)=0$, so the ring map $j$ vanishes on $IB$ and induces a ring map $\rho:B/IB\to F$ with $\rho(\bar b)=j(b)$. Then $e:=\rho(\varepsilon)$ is an idempotent of $F$ and $1-e=\rho(1-\varepsilon)=j(u)$. Also $j(\varphi(a))=\varphi(a)\otimes1=1\otimes(a\cdot1)$, i.e. $j\circ\varphi$ is the composite $A\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to F$.

source.place: more-algebra.tex:2512-2516, proof of Lemma Tag 09XH (lemma-helper-finite-type), first sentence ('by looking at fibre rings, see Algebra, Definition 00PL'); details written out by the worker

proof.text: The prime $\mathfrak Q$ of the fibre ring. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection] (applied to $\varphi$, $\mathfrak p$ and the prime $\mathfrak q$, which satisfies $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$) there is a unique prime $\mathfrak Q\subset F$ with $j^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)=\mathfrak q$; it is the prime of $F$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q$. Since $u\in\mathfrak q$ (step 1), $1-e=j(u)\in\mathfrak Q$ (step 2).

source.place: more-algebra.tex:2512-2516, proof of Lemma Tag 09XH (lemma-helper-finite-type), first sentence ('by looking at fibre rings, see Algebra, Definition 00PL'); details written out by the worker

proof.text: $F/(1-e)F$ is a finite $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra. Let $\bar F=F/(1-e)F$, a $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra via $\lambda\mapsto1\otimes\lambda$. As $b\otimes\lambda=\lambda\cdot(b\otimes1)$, $F$ is spanned over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ by the $j(b)$, $b\in B$, so $\bar F$ is spanned by their classes. Since $j(b)(1-e)\in(1-e)F$, the class of $j(b)$ equals the class of $j(b)e=\rho(\bar b\varepsilon)$. Let $c_1,\dots,c_n\in\varepsilon(B/IB)=C_1$ generate $C_1$ as an $A/I$-module, where $\bar a\in A/I$ acts by multiplication by $\varepsilon\bar\varphi(\bar a)$. Then $\bar b\varepsilon\in C_1$ is $\sum_i\varepsilon\bar\varphi(\bar a_i)c_i=\sum_i\bar\varphi(\bar a_i)c_i$ for some $a_i\in A$, so $\rho(\bar b\varepsilon)=\sum_ij(\varphi(a_i))\rho(c_i)=\sum_i(a_i\cdot1_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)})\cdot\rho(c_i)$ by step 2. Hence the classes of $\rho(c_1),\dots,\rho(c_n)$ span $\bar F$ over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$: $\bar F$ is a finite $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra.

source.place: more-algebra.tex:2512-2516, proof of Lemma Tag 09XH (lemma-helper-finite-type), first sentence ('by looking at fibre rings, see Algebra, Definition 00PL'); details written out by the worker

proof.text: The primes of $F$ containing $1-e$. The field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a local ring whose only prime ideal is its maximal ideal $0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum] (with $R=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and the finite $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra $\bar F$ of step 4), $\bar F$ has only finitely many prime ideals, each of them maximal. By the correspondence between ideals of $F$ containing $(1-e)F$ and ideals of $\bar F$, the primes of $F$ containing $1-e$ are the preimages of the primes of $\bar F$, and such a prime $\mathfrak Q'$ is maximal in $F$ because $F/\mathfrak Q'\cong\bar F/(\mathfrak Q'/(1-e)F)$ is a field. So $V(1-e)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(F)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is a finite set of maximal ideals, containing $\mathfrak Q$ (step 3); each of its points $\mathfrak M$ is closed in $\operatorname{Spec}(F)$, as $\{\mathfrak M\}=V(\mathfrak M)$.

source.place: more-algebra.tex:2512-2516, proof of Lemma Tag 09XH (lemma-helper-finite-type), first sentence ('by looking at fibre rings, see Algebra, Definition 00PL'); details written out by the worker

proof.text: $\mathfrak Q$ is isolated. A prime of $F$ contains exactly one of $e$ and $1-e$: not both, since $e+(1-e)=1$, and at least one, since $e(1-e)=0$. So $V(1-e)=D(e)$, which is open in $\operatorname{Spec}(F)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent] (applied to the idempotent $e$ of $F$). The set $W=V(1-e)\setminus\{\mathfrak Q\}$ is a finite union of closed points (step 5), hence closed. Therefore $\{\mathfrak Q\}=D(e)\cap(\operatorname{Spec}(F)\setminus W)$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}(F)$: $\mathfrak Q$ is an isolated point of $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p))$.

source.place: more-algebra.tex:2512-2516, proof of Lemma Tag 09XH (lemma-helper-finite-type), first sentence ('by looking at fibre rings, see Algebra, Definition 00PL'); details written out by the worker

proof.text: Conclusion. $A\to B$ is of finite type and the prime $\mathfrak Q$ of $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q$ (step 3) is an isolated point of its spectrum (step 6); by [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime] (Stacks 00PL via 00PK (1)) $A\to B$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$. As $\mathfrak q\in T$ was arbitrary, this holds at every prime of $T$.

split_report.summary: Checked against Stacks more-algebra.tex 2512-2516 (Tag 09XH, first sentence of the proof) and algebra.tex 30195-30241 (Tags 00PK, 00PL); verified the tags in tags/tags. The affine notion 'quasi-finite at a prime' had no node (pqf-def-quasifinite is the scheme definition and only refers to it), so a definition node def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime (00PL with 00PK (1), isolated point of Spec(S tensor kappa(p))) was created and the statement now cites it. The statement was made precise: T is defined as the image of Spec(C_1) under pi: B -> C_1 (Stacks calls T closed; the old text called it 'closed-and-open over V(I)'), and the conclusion is spelled out. Proof written out in 7 steps: I in p and a lift u of 1-epsilon lies in q; B/IB -> F = B tensor kappa(p) and the idempotent e; the prime Q of F over q via lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection, with 1-e in Q; F/(1-e)F finite over kappa(p) by a spanning argument; its primes finite and maximal via the leaf lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum; V(1-e)=D(e) open via lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent, so {Q} open. Tag 00PM (the finite-fibre criterion named in the old statement) is not needed and was dropped from the statement. Mathlib: no match for the item; Algebra.quasiFiniteAt_iff_isOpen_singleton_fiber (RingTheory/ZariskisMainTheorem.lean:754) is the bridge to Mathlib's Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt.
